change: Added Sternal Head to primary chest latins alongside Clavicular Head. The landmine press uses a diagonal angle similar to a low-incline press, engaging both chest heads (clavicular dominant but sternal also active). Removed Lateral Deltoids from secondary — a sagittal-plane diagonal press does not meaningfully recruit lateral deltoids; anterior deltoid is the shoulder prime mover. Added oblique secondary to reflect anti-rotation core demand of the standing bilateral press.
No changes. Obliques primary, lower back and abs secondary — confirmed correct by web search.
No changes. Flat bench with legs extended: chest (sternal dominant, both heads) primary, triceps and anterior deltoids primary, abs and obliques secondary — all confirmed correct.

Moved Hamstrings from primary to secondary. Research and CLAUDE.md rules both confirm hamstrings are secondary (stabilising/synergist) in squats, including low bar squats. Even though low bar activates hamstrings more than high bar, hamstring MVIC during squats is typically 20% or less — they assist glutes in hip extension but are not prime movers. Quads and Gluteus Maximus remain primary.

Restructured primary upper body: removed shoulders (Anterior Deltoids, Lateral Deltoids) from primary and moved to secondary — deltoids assist and stabilise the catch but are not prime movers of the lift. Separated mid back primary to Upper Traps only (the explosive shrug is the primary upper-body action); removed Rhomboids from primary (they stabilise the scapula but are secondary movers). Added Rhomboids to secondary mid back merged into a secondary entry. Kept quads, glutes, hamstrings as primary (full triple extension = prime movers). Added forearms (Wrist Flexors) to secondary for grip demand. Calves plantarflexion is a meaningful contributor to triple extension but cannot be confirmed as primary vs secondary — left as secondary was not added due to 5-secondary cap already reached; omitted calves to keep entries to 5 secondary slots. Uncertainty: calves (Gastrocnemius) participate in triple extension — could be argued secondary.
